text_fidelity_a:
Belkin N300 Wireless N Router (Latest Generation) (F9K1002) Bought this for my mother who has a small 2 bedroom apartment. Has been installed for over 3 weeks now. It was so very easy to install, simple instructions, did not have to adjust any settings. We just attached it to the DSL modem, loaded the CD into each computer that was going to use the network, followed the simple instructions, works great. We did have a problem trying to set up an account, which we still have not been able to do. May call later for assistance if we find it would be helpful to have an account, but so far everything works great.

We have had my mother's desktop computer (also running wireless now), her notebook computer, my notebook computer and the printer all running on the network at the same time. There was absolutely no degradation in service, have never had a problem with disconnects even with all computers running at the same time and two of the computers sending documents to the printer. This includes using one of the notebook computers at the furthest location in the apartment away from the router as possible. The only problem we have is the slower Verizon DSL service compared to the faster Verizon FIOS service I have at my house, so not a Belkin problem. Too bad my mother can't get FIOS. But her internet access is as fast as it was when it was attached directly to the modem.

Would highly recommend this product.

5/28/2015 - Just found this review I wrote in 2011. My mother is still using the same Belkin N150, still works great even if we have 3 computers running at the same time. The retirement community she lives in switched voice/Internet carriers about 6 months ago. Saw no difference in performance. Highly recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Belkin N300 Wireless N Router (Latest Generation) (F9K1002)

text_fidelity_a:
Aftershokz AS450 Sportz M3 Mobile Bone Conduction Headphones with Microphone (Black) purchased for single sided hearing loss after extensive research for "the best" on the market (at this or near this price point).
perks:
i can hear more clearly out of that ear using this headset. (music, netflix dialogue). if you're not deaf in one ear, this is irrelevant.
Can listen while charging, so no "down time" like some other products.
cons:
headset is uncomfortable in multiple positions. i can not really find a good position, but the least uncomfortable- and interestingly enough, the best sound quality is NOT in manufacture explained position: it's over my head with the pods near my temples or behind my ears.
Sound quality is not good, it's better coming through tinny computer speakers, but using those, i can only hear it well on my good ear. It's louder/better/and more clear (can hear fine details in the music) if you wear a headband or tight hat to press the pods against your head- but again comfort is a factor.
Noise leak is a major factor. If you turn it up to "low-normal" listening volume (cell phone set at half volume, headset set to lowest selectable volume) my housemate can still hear music played at arms reach. do not anticipate that you can wear it around others in a quiet room.

would i buy again? no.
Did I return them due to problems as stated above. Yeah.
text_fidelity_b: Aftershokz AS450 Sportz M3 Mobile Bone Conduction Headphones with Microphone (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Monster ScreenClean Soft Touch Wipes, Screen Cleaner Wipes for Computer Screens, TV, Phones, Tablets, and Car Touch Screens, Home Office, 70 Count After 40-some years on the technical side of electrochemical fabrication (12" wafer fab) and manufacturing that included the IBM PS1 & PS2 birth … cleanliness is Godliness. I've likely tried every chemical variant of cleaner ever invented, though many fewer are now permitted for USA use.

Though impractical for the laptop, some excellent cleaners in the $1000/gal category might be suggested for cleansing strategic missile-related monitors and surfaces. The value and reliability of what device you are cleaning is the most critical consideration when choosing a cleaner. A wrong choice might pay back immediately with bad results, dissolving the anti-reflective coating or lamination of the touch screen overlay, removing specialized keyboard paints, ruining distinctive finishes, etc. For another, that same choice might do a bang-up job on the big screen at home, but when used on a laptop, it slowly dissolves and/or corrodes critical interconnects as you pass through dewpoints on that 17-hour airplane ride to Sydney.

Q: What is the best cleaner to shine on my $1500 laptop?

A: Not the cheapest $4/qt cleaner. Not one of grandma's window elixirs.

Behind the scenes, there is likely no other technical discussion as critical as cleaning and cleaners. Billions are spent every year on the problem. What I know from experience is that an alcohol solvent-based cleaner does a pretty good job erasing the symbology that makes my lighted keyboard legible. I look for a cleaner to remove the latent crusty-goo residue left by that anti-viral covid computer cleaner six months ago. Some cleaners with notionally benign saponifiers that sell under the enviro-friendly, "Green!", "non-GMO!" moniker is known to corrode solder joints and electro-plating to short the keyboard and LCD/OLED out.

Finding the right balance between solvent and saponifiers has not evolved smoothly. Saponifiers remove organics. The stuff that sprays out of your mouth and nose when yelling at the laptop. Solvents remove inorganics like hand cream, french fry grease, and Cheeto dust. I've rolled up all of this wisdom in my 'Rule #446 - Do not buy the cheapest electronics cleaner. Ever.'

This Monster cleaner is not cheap. It's a premium cleaner under a known premium brand. Given Monster brands, cleaning processes are the #1 priority for their established long-lived high-fidelity interconnection. My laptop has a touch screen that demands a non-delaminating cleaner and a lighted keyboard with that funky paint and laser-etched symbology. This Monster cleaner did an unexpectedly quick, no-smudge job on the laptop. All is good.
text_fidelity_b: Monster ScreenClean Soft Touch Wipes, Screen Cleaner Wipes for Computer Screens, TV, Phones, Tablets, and Car Touch Screens, Home Office, 70 Count

Headphone for Men This is a great idea: the combination of a USB 3.0 hub and a gigabit adapter. It's a perfect space-saving option -- the overall size is just a bit larger than my gigabit adapter and I get 3 USB 3.0 ports as a bonus!

The build quality is very good. It seems odd to use the word "stylish" to describe such a device, but this is quite stylish -- the case is black with a steel gray brushed top (which looks like metal, but I believe it is plastic). The case is sturdy and has tight seams, and the USB and RJ45 ports are well-anchored. The connection cable is short (about one foot long) but very stout with an well-made USB connector on the PC end.

Setup is quick and easy. The hub portion is a straight plus-and-play install on Win 7 (and, I would imagine, other Windows versions as well). The Ethernet adapter requires drivers, which are supplied on an included CD-ROM (which I'm pleased to report is a full-size CD rather than those mini ones which are such a pain to use).

The hub is passive (no external power) so there are limitations as to what it can support. I didn't have any problems using it with low power draws, such as thumb drives.

It comes with a brief, but well-written user guide.

Well-made, works great, and a easy, compact way to add two different functions to a laptop (or any other PC). Highly recommend.
[Sample provided for review]

The screen is sharp and readable in 2240 x 1400 pixels mode. This model does NOT have a touch screen, so if that's important to you, you need to look at other laptops that sport that feature. The system so far is quick to respond to requests and has sufficient RAM and storage space.

One nice feature missing from all the other laptops I’ve owned or used is an automatic power up whenever the computer case is opened. There is also a power button in case you need it.

Beside Windows 11 Pro, this machine comes with significant value added: a year subscription to Microsoft Office 365 (normally $69.99/year) and also a two-year subscription to McAfee LiveSafe security suite (normally $129.99/year).

Most people who use laptops probably don’t mind that this machine, like most laptops now, does not have an ethernet port. However, WiFi seems to be performing well in its absence. I may not be the typical user, but I prefer the option to connect by ethernet.

I work almost exclusively at a desk with the power supply connected, so I have not tested the battery life of this Dell. My only real complaint is that, owing to the 14” display size, the keyboard is correspondingly smaller than I like. If I were to do much typing, I’d probably plug in an external keyboard. If your hands are smaller than mine are, this won't be much of an issue for you.

As has been mentioned in other reviews, this is not a gamer’s dream machine. It’s for normal office and business use. Its compact size makes it good for the road.

AcuRite Iris (5-in-1) Indoor/Outdoor Wireless Weather Station for Indoor and Outdoor Temperature and Humidity, Wind Speed and Direction, and Rainfall with Digital Display (01512M) Purchased the Acu-rite 5-in-1 weather station June 11, 2018.

Unit ceased communicating with the base unit in November 2021.

Had Energizer Lithium AA cells installed. Changed out to new AA alkaline cells. No communication with base unit.

Changed "A-B-C" channel from "C" to "A". Still no communication.

The unit has no capability of wifi to my phone.

Display is very very bright. Lights up the whole kitchen/living room. May be too bright for some, though there are three levels of brightness.

I think my next weather station will have a predominantly dark display instead of this predominantly bright display. The new device will also connect to my phone.

To its credit, it has operated in impossibly high Arizona desert temperatures where it read 121 degrees. I'm sure the unit itself was hotter as it was sitting in the blistering sun all day for several years.

Still, being a weather station, one would assume it's *designed* to sit out in all manner of weather, no matter how hot or cold.

text_fidelity_a:
Canon EF 100mm f/2.8 Macro USM Fixed Lens for Canon SLR Cameras Although this lens is intended for macro photography, it's also a great lens for general purpose shots, or portrait shots. The lens produces beautiful sharp images and is a fast, accurate focuser. The lens is moderately heavy and bulky, so I wouldn't classify it as eminently carryable, and without image stabilization, you might suffer hand shake blur if you're not shooting at the wide end; at smaller apertures, using it with a tripod is highly recommended. But if you're buying it primarily to get into macro this shouldn't much matter as tripod shooting with macro is virtually a necessity, and completely expected.

The 100mm focal length is a nice compromise when you want to get close to small subjects (particularly insects) but are limited to how close you can get before scaring the subject off - as a comparison with the 180mm macro, you would want to factor in a consideration as to what you might like to shoot most of the time - big spiders that you'd rather stay well away from might be an application more suited to the 180mm, for instance, but if you are keen to shoot mostly flowers, the 180 might be more length than you really need.

In short, the 100mm macro is one of my "keeper" lenses, a real performer.
text_fidelity_b: Canon EF 100mm f/2.8 Macro USM Fixed Lens for Canon SLR Cameras

text_fidelity_a:
Bose Companion 20 Multimedia Speaker System Silver I wanted a set of speakers to use mainly for my Kindle Fire and MP3 player, but also as my computer speakers. Due to space constraints, a 2.0 system was my only option, since a subwoofer (regardless of the size) would be problematic.

So the search began. There were several speakers that sounded great, including the Creative Gigaworks, M Audio and Audioengine. However, they lacked the convenience features I wanted such as ease of connecting/disconnecting a tablet and volume control without having to reach out and touch the speaker.

The Bose Companion 20 initially caught my eye because of the control pod. That was a great solution to my problems since I could control the volume right on my desk plus have the ability to plug in/unplug a tablet very easily. The sound quality sealed the deal - everyone who hears these speakers think they are a 2.1 set due to the ample bass. But, the bass is not at the expense of clear mid and upper ranges.

I use these 60% for music and 40% for video, and for both applications, the sound quality has been just wonderful. I'm also impressed that they sound just as good with the volume dialed way down as they do at moderate or blast-out-the-walls loud.

The control pod is very well made. It has a nice weight to it and a non-skid backing so it stays put. The volume control works very smoothly with a solid feel. I'm especially fond of being able to turn the speakers on and off by just touching the control pod.

You can connect it to the PC and to an aux device (such as a tablet) and use both at the same time. That's important since I want to listen to music or a video from my Fire, but still want to hear a chime when an email arrives.

My complaints are that the control pod cable is a bit too short for my needs. It's about 5 foot long, which is ample if you have the speakers next to your PC, but I have my speakers on a shelf above my desk. I was able to arrange things to make it work, but another foot or two of cable (or the ability to purchase an extension) would have been nice. It's a custom cable, so an off-the-shelf extension is not possible.

My other complaint is the price. I was able to get a used pair for half of the regular price. I think these are a bit overpriced at the regular price. But, Bose hit a really unique niche - the ability to have great sound without any compromise in convenience. If you want both, there's a high cost for admission.

If the price is not an issue, these very much deserve a hard look if you're in the market for a great sounding pair of 2.0 speakers. Highly recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Bose Companion 20 Multimedia Speaker System Silver

I keep one on me, one in a safe at my house, one in a safety deposit box and another with a trusted friend that has no idea what it goes to. These things are the best protection you can own for logging in to accounts using MFA.

Wall Outlet Extender Surge Protector - 6 Outlet Wall Adapter with 3 USB Charging Ports (1 USB-C, 2 USB A), Multi Plug Outlets Wall Mount with Top Phone Holder for Home, Dorm Essentail, 490 Joules There has been an unpleasant shift, from who is responsible for supplying the power adapters for USB powered appliances. And, for the number of simple household appliances that now require those adapters. I suppose that I can see the logic in it. Newer electrical devices now require lower power. Thence, adapters. At first, they came with the device, like cell phones were supplied with the wall adapters. Eventually, you had to buy your own adapters. Even now, you have to be careful in selecting an adapter. There are basic ones that only have 3 amps. Some have 5 amps or more. Some only split all their power between multiple ports. Some are 'smart' and provide all the amps needed to multiple devices. Now, that's pretty much the rule. You gotta do it yourself and you better know what you're looking for. Disappointment is more common than satisfaction, in this new game.

These outlet adapters from Mifusa probably wouldn't have been my optimum choice, had the listing been a little more informative. But, based on what I read and how it works, it will do well enough.

The six outlets are too close together for bulky plugs or those that have the transformers built into the plugs. The total amperage across all three USB ports is only 3 amps. So, don't look to power multiple USB devices efficiently. BUT, you CAN plug six AC (that's alternating current, not air conditioning) of a low enough power draw, and three USB powered devices, IF they will all fit in the MIFUSA device, and know that they also have surge protection, as indicated by the little green light.

One star being crap and five stars being spectacular, I rate these as being 'okay'.
text_fidelity_b: Wall Outlet Extender Surge Protector - 6 Outlet Wall Adapter with 3 USB Charging Ports (1 USB-C, 2 USB A), Multi Plug Outlets Wall Mount with Top Phone Holder for Home, Dorm Essentail, 490 Joules

I own 3 varieties of BOSE headphones, and I needed to get a new headset with a USB connection since my work laptop is broken in that I can hear web calls but not speak. I'll address some conflicting reviews that I found to be bunk:
Comfort - I'm usually not a fan of on-ear headsets but these are padded and comfy. They aren't too light as to slip off, nor are they heavy or bulky. One reviewer said the cord and control circle (volume and mute) was so heavy as to drag the headphones off his head ... totally untrue. The cord is very long - you can slide over to your file cabinet or printer - yay. And the cord is NOT heavy as to feel its weight on that side of the headset.
Sound - The sound is excellent and as I mentioned, I'm a BOSE girl. There are so many USB headsets in the $39 - $79 range and I'm glad I spent the extra dollars for this price point. Working from home in the COVID age means a lot more WebEx and Zoom meetings, and sound - and noise cancellation - has to be excellent. One reviewer said she could hear herself breathing. That only happens when the mouthpiece is aimed at your nostril - duh. Move it.

I can't comment on longevity as these are new, but hopefully these will have a nice long usage life.

text_fidelity_a:
SanDisk Ultra Fit 16GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive SDCZ43-016G-G46 I have a macbook pro with only 126gb of capacity in the SSD. This is not enough for someone who does photography and graphics design.
Unfortunately, with the new MBPs, apple decided that the user should not be allowed to change out their SSD for a larger capacity after purchase.
This caused a lot of problems and I was constantly transferring my images to an external HDD and it was extremely inconvenient.

I decided to purchase this USB flash drive. It was low cost for such a large amount of space. Best decision I ever made!
I have had this in my laptop for the last 2 months and it has not fallen out or gotten damaged. I carry my laptop everywhere with me.
Data transfers are very fast. With less than 50 picutures, it's basically instant and I often feel the need to check and make sure the files actually transferred because it happens so quickly, I don't even get a "Transferring files" window. I have never had a failed transfer.

If you are using it in a mac, you will need to reformat it to ExFAT. It will work out of the box, but will not accept large folders or files until it is reformatted.

The only issue I've ever had is if my computer falls asleep, the drive will sometimes disconnect, but that is due to the settings on my computer and not the drive. A simple unplug-replug reconnects it.
text_fidelity_b: SanDisk Ultra Fit 16GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive SDCZ43-016G-G46

text_fidelity_a:
SABRENT USB 2.0 to DB25 IEEE 1284 Parallel Printer Cable Adapter [HEXNUT Connectors] (CB-1284) Although every new printer has a USB port, I have a few older, but still perfectly functioning printers that only have parallel inputs. I've been using those printers with PCs that have a parallel output port but, as those PCs get retired, it's getting harder to find a way to hook up the old printers. This solves that problem very well.

It's a simple cable. One end is a USB plug; the other is a DB25 female parallel port. IMPORTANT: you want to check your printer to make sure it can accept a DB25 female plug. Many printers only have a 36-pin Centronics input. If so, you need to get this one: [[ASIN:B00IDU0T1Y Sabrent USB to Parallel IEEE 1284 Printer Cable Adapter (CB-CN36)]]

The cable itself is decent. Thin, but the jacket feels more than sturdy enough for the job at hand. It's only 6 foot long which is OK for my needs but just barely. A longer version (10 or 12 foot) would be nice.

Works fine, and no complaints.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: SABRENT USB 2.0 to DB25 IEEE 1284 Parallel Printer Cable Adapter [HEXNUT Connectors] (CB-1284)

Technology has advanced during those years, though, and this device is a bit more sophisticated in some ways than my old Bluetooth.

Just like my old Bluetooth, this one claims to have 11 hours of battery life when fully charged, and just like my old Bluetooth, its charge doesn’t last nearly that long. However, this model fully rechargs fairly rapidly, in under an hour, much faster than my old Bluetooth.

If I have this particular style of Bluetooth in my ear more than an hour, my ear gets sore. But the good news is that the ear hook allows it to stay firmly in place, even if bending over or exercising.

This Bluetooth pairs easily. I haven’t tried to pair it simultaneously with more than one phone, though the manufacturer claims it has that capability.

The sound quality is good not only for listening to calls and being heard clearly on the other end of a call, it is also good enough to listen to podcasts, audiobooks or music. However, other than for receiving or making calls, I much prefer other styles of Bluetooth to this one for listening to entertainment media, because I can keep their ear pieces in my ears for hours without discomfort, unlike this type of design.

I purchased this just to use as a slave to be triggered by another flash - a Yongnuo 560-II. I figured this one looked pretty similar and cost a lot less (though it's less powerful and doesn't have zooming or an LCD screen, doesn't go into sleep mode. I didn't need those things). If you're shooting your nephew's 5th Birthday Party and don't care if the shots come out (why aren't you using a phone cam?), then this is OK. Sabrent SB-256-EC-NVME-BLK 256Gb NVMe USB 3.1 External Aluminum SSD The Sabrent External SSD honestly saved my day. My MacBook Pro’s display developed funky lines out of the blue, so it had to go in for a hardware repair. I write and save everything on my hard drive, so naturally I wanted a ton of backups. Just in case the worst happened and I ended up losing everything during the repair.

My appointment was set up for the next day, so I had little time to make a ton of backups. AND there was a massive thunderstorm, so the power kept flickering. I tried a normal stick first, and the estimated time was like 3 HOURS to copy everything. I so didn’t have time for that. I plugged the Sabrent in, started the copy, and went to get a drink. When I came back in less than five minutes, it was finished!!

I just now copied a 16gb folder in 48.15 seconds.

The USB-C adapter on the cord is also very handy, if you use the Sabrent on several computers or other devices. When I use the Sabrent on my MacBook Pro, I’m unable to plug anything else into the neighboring USB port because the adapter is blocky. But I’ll take the convenience of having one on the cord rather than having to go hunt for an adapter in my office.

The SSD itself is quite small. Very portable. The box the SSD comes in is great for storing the drive between uses, too. There’s a slightly padded interior compartment and a spot for the cord.

Philips MANT940 UHF Digital and Analog Indoor/Outdoor Antenna (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I'm within ten miles of 13 transmitters, but on the far slope (for most) of a densely-wooded hill. I used to get pretty good reception from an old aluminum christmas-tree type attic-mounted (non-amplified) antenna, but broke it accidentally. This amplified MANT940 is just as good, and a WHOLE lot smaller and easier to manipulate!

Attached to my Philips 5603D, this device (and 25 feet of extension cable) is providing me with 31 digital channels!?! Not always perfectly clearly (that is, there's occasional smear and freezing), but it's attached to an outside wall next to a window and easy to tweak - there's probably a better position, but this is convenient. So far I'm also getting 11 analog channels, but they're all dups. Some of the digital ones are pure advertising, and not all are HDTV, but WHOA - CBS! UNbelievable high def picture, and GREAT signal (WHYY sucks.) Beat THIS price, Comcast/FiOS!

BTW, I can now say most channels give great signal - even in a snowstorm!!!

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Paperwhite 3G, 6" High Resolution Display with Built-in Light, Free 3G + Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers [Previous Generation - 5th] I have always loved the Keyboard version (and still do), but unfortunately without the benefit of backlighting and the poor selection of cases with adequate lighting (I've ordered and returned several), I started to use it less and less - and used my Iphone App almost exclusively. But I really wanted to use a Kindle which was designed primarily for reading books as opposed to the small screen of a Smart phone. And I'm not about to go lugging around an Ipad day after day.

Last year I purchased a Kindle Touch but was extremely unhappy with the instability of the touch screen and other issues with that model. So I bought the aforementioned Keyboard and made do with it. I should add that I have owned five Kindles since their launch in 2007. When the Paperwhite was announced, I immediately got one for my husband while I waited for a 3g model for myself.

Initially I was a little disappointed with the Paperwhite because of my own lack of patience and constant comparing it to my other devices. I had to get use to swiping the screen to wake it up, understand the basic settings operations, and generally become comfortable with this model. I have to admit that I had contacted Amazon about sending it back within a couple of days of receiving it, but for some reason (maybe maturity?), I decided to keep it for another few days just to play with it a bit more.

I am so glad that I did. My only complaint is that I wish Amazon would have included some kind of cheat sheet to get users started. It would have gone a long way to prevent my initial meltdown. If my husband hadn't had his own Paperwhite for a month and shown me all of the basics, I can assure you that this model would be back in the hands of Amazon employees right now. They don't need to include some overwhelming instruction manual. Just one piece of paper with some simple "how to" notes would be perfect - I'd even be willing to draft something up for them!

Now that I've settled down with my Paperwhite, and have begun to take advantage of the outstanding benefits that it offers (i.e. instant dictionary, reading in the dark, lightweight and gorgeous, etc.) I would not part with it for anything. And my Keyboard is about to become a special gift to a friend who has always wanted a Kindle.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Paperwhite 3G, 6" High Resolution Display with Built-in Light, Free 3G + Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers [Previous Generation - 5th]

text_fidelity_a:
ZUGU CASE - 2019 iPad Air 10.5/2017 iPad Pro 10.5 inch Case Prodigy X - Very Protective But Thin + Convenient Magnetic Stand + Sleep/Wake Cover (Purple) Update: A good pencil sleeve to use with this case after stretching it out a bit with a crayola dry erase marker is the Hydream Silicone Case for Apple Pencil Holder Sleeve Skin Pocket Cover Accessories for iPad Pro 9.7/10.5/12.9, Cute Soft Grip Pouch with Charging Cap Holder and 2 Protective Nib Covers.

TL:DR - a fantastic case and looks amazing with a screen protector on the device. Does not interfere with screen protectors at all. Great utility and angle options. Looks good on the fridge too. If you don't mind the case feeling a bit awkward to hold when looking at things in portrait and the fact that your Pencil Sleeve options are limited due to the super tight elastic (I used a crayola dry eraser to stretch mine and now the fit perfect) this is the case for you.

Pros:
8 Adjustment points
The packaging and info included on the company
The quality
The looks (at least in black for me)
The pencil sleeve built in
The wake/sleep utility
Solid positions minus the last one if you're really pretty on it. Like heavy handed drawing hard.

Cons:
The tablet is hard to hold in portrait especially if the pencil is in the case
I know the 2018 Pro model had yet to be released when this case was made, but I wish the placement of the Pencil sleeve was in a better location or allowed enough space for a wider variety of pencil sleeves. It makes me worry that it sticks out a little from the case. Kinda wish it was on the top or had a similar elastic sleeve loop on the top where an Apple Pencil 2 would sit magnetically. More or a nitpick though.
The tightness of the sleeve out of the box! This was very annoying, but another nitpick since I can always stretch it out.
A little awkward to use the rear-facing camera since when holding with the front panel touching the back of the case it covers the camera completely. Even when in landscape you have to tilt it high enough to free your view.

Quality of Life Cons: (basically super nitpicks. Feel free to ignore. The case is great!)
Would have been nice if they added another small sleeve near the rear pencil sleeve for the small charging Pencil dongle. It looks like there is enough room in the back.
Like the little indents where the power and volume buttons are located I'd have liked to see a little notch above the charging port center of the charging port. Why? Because I often find myself inserting the connector low of the actual charging port and a little notch where the middle would generally be would have been a nice touch or at least some more material to alleviate confusion on the port's location. If you look at the charging port with the case on you'll see what I mean, there is a little lip which can make it confusing on what I'm inserting the plug into (done this a lot lately, but getting better at it).
A somewhat more rigid hinge on the panel that covers the screen. Why? It can get really floppy when holding it in portrait mode and a slightly more rigid hinge kind of like the surface pro keyboard cover would have been nice. The panel itself is solid but the material connecting it to the case can be a little floppy.
text_fidelity_b: ZUGU CASE - 2019 iPad Air 10.5/2017 iPad Pro 10.5 inch Case Prodigy X - Very Protective But Thin + Convenient Magnetic Stand + Sleep/Wake Cover (Purple)

text_fidelity_a:
SABRENT 4TB Rocket NVMe PCIe M.2 2280 Internal SSD High Performance Solid State Drive (SB-ROCKET-4TB) So, I've had this thing for a few months, and it is no longer working. I put my OS (Win10) on it, and everything seemed fine. The NVMe has a heat shield on it that has a fan, so the temps never got as high as some people have reported.

However, the performance of my computer slowly declined until I could no longer rely on the computer to not crash randomly within 30 minutes of starting it. Everything was failing. I could not figure out what the heck was going on. Started troubleshooting everything. Couldn't get through a memtest, so I bought some new ram so I can use my computer while I wait for the G.Skill RMA process. However, even with the new ram, the PC cannot boot with the Sabrent NVMe. Does not proceed further than the loading screen.

Tried booting into safe mode, which failed, as well as resetting the computer through the windows troubleshooting tool. Nothing would go past the loading screen. I've added another photo showing that substantial loss of performance, even while it is not being used by anything else. Keep in mind that although the numbers are mostly higher than the SATA SSD, a loss in performance like this is a tell-tale sign that it is failing. If you notice something similar with your hardware, back up what you want to keep immediately.

Tried booting from my older SSD, and was able to boot just fine. I am still somehow able to access the information on the NVMe when booting from another SSD, but the system is unstable while running on it. I will continue to try to get a replacement or a refund before conceding that I have a $120 tax for trying to save money.

I tried to use the tool to check if there was a firmware update. Doesn't work, as it said cannot find information on the hardware. This is with the latest everything. Seemed odd, so I sent an email to the bug reporting email they provide. Got a response from google saying that email does not exist....

I reached out to Sabrent technical support. No response after a week.

I'm very disappointed. I've gotten other sabrent hardware before and hadn't had problems. Looks like their memory is not their game. Even worse that their customer support is non-existent. Don't expect to get help if you run into the same issue that I got.

I'd recommend spending the extra $20 or $30 to get hardware that has a record of reliability, like samsung (the much older SSD that still works, and and using right now to be able to even use my computer is the 840 EVO).
text_fidelity_b: SABRENT 4TB Rocket NVMe PCIe M.2 2280 Internal SSD High Performance Solid State Drive (SB-ROCKET-4TB)

text_fidelity_a:
Monoprice Active Indoor/Outdoor HD6 HDTV Antenna, 50 Mile Range, Video Antenna (115953) Black Before you buy, check the Monoprice website for this item. The price may be much cheaper over there.

This is a very inexpensive, relatively low quality TV antenna. You get what you pay for. They advertise this for both indoor and outdoor use, but the mostly plastic construction will not last long outdoors in areas that get a lot of wind, ice, or bright sunlight. The attached 3 foot cable really tells you what their intended use case is. If your TV is near a window, hang the antenna in the window, plug it in, and you're done.

The advertised 50 mile range is for ideal conditions, mounting the antenna outdoors in an area where there are absolutely no obstructions between your home and the TV broadcast tower (no trees, no buildings, etc). Expect much worse range for an indoor mounting and if there are any obstructions. If you live in an area with trees etc, you should get a more sturdy antenna that can be mounted on a pole on top of your roof so it can receive a signal over the trees.

This antenna is advertised for UHF frequencies only. Most TV stations use UHF these days, but in my area there are a couple that use VHF and this antenna is not usable for those channels. If you really want VHF, I suggest getting a different antenna from this one.
text_fidelity_b: Monoprice Active Indoor/Outdoor HD6 HDTV Antenna, 50 Mile Range, Video Antenna (115953) Black

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Oasis – With 7” display and page turn buttons- Ad-Supported + 3 Months Free Kindle Unlimited (with auto-renewal) [[VIDEOID:a23b5cd930e819bd2cae7872ede2dd37]] I decided to finally upgrade my Kindle from the first Paperwhite when I found out I could get a 25% discount and a $5 Amazon gift card for trading in my very old and unused Kindle Keyboard 1st gen, as well as other bonuses of 6 months free Kindle Unlimited (approx $60) plus a 30 day Audible trial.

I’m very happy with it and it has some great features.
I do like the adjustable amber tint, but I also really like the ability to invert the colors to white print on a black background. This is even easier on the eyes, but it does have a noticeable (and irritating) white flash every few page turns when using the buttons, and almost with every page turn when advancing with the touch screen. I believe this is the e-ink refreshing. I will probably use the black inverted color only when I’m reading outside in bright sunlight.

I also am really happy to have buttons to turn the page again. It’s the ultimate laziness to be able to just keep your thumb in the button and depress it to turn the page instead of having to actually move your thumb a half inch to touch the screen, but hey, why move a half inch when your can push down 1/16th of an inch? All that extra movement add up over the years.
The real reason I like the buttons is this: I live in Alaska and we have very long, cold nights. But even in the winter, we turn down the heat at night. I read in bed every single night, tucked all cozy and warm under my down comforter... except for having to have my hand out in order to touch the screen on my Paperwhite to turn the page. My hand starts to get very cold. It’s uncomfortable. My half frozen hand takes away from my happy bedtime reading experience. With the Oasis, I can keep my hand under the blankets and just push the button. You don’t know what a big deal this is until you spend night after night with a frozen hand.

I also like that you can select which button to the the page advance button and which is the page back button. The Oasis comes set up with the top button as the page advance and the bottom as the page back, but I switched them: the bottom is the advance, the top is the back. I hold my ereaders at the bottom sides, and had to stretch my thumb to advance the page when it was set for the top button. It’s just easier and more comfortable to use the bottom button. And this is cool: the bottom button stays as my page advance button even when I rotate the Oasis 180 to use left handed!! Smart!!

Others have covered the size and weight so I won’t go it I all that except to say it’s comfortable to hold. I do use the official Amazon Premium leather cover and it fits perfectly, and the magnetic closure/sleep/wake functions work perfectly also.

Dislike: Nothing with the ereader itself, but with however Amazon picks the “special offers”. From what I read, these offers are supposed to be tailored off of a person’s reading history/preferences. I may be wrong.
The books they are featuring for me are “romance” genre. I am sooo not a romance genre girl. I don’t believe I’ve ever purchased this genre in my life. I’m a hardcore sci-fi/dystopian. I have an adverse reaction when I see romance special offer.

Other than that, some of the complaints by others leaves me wondering.
I just don’t think it’s THAT big of deal that it has a micro usb. Really, it’s just not that hard to figure out the big end of the cable from the small end. As for charging speed, charge mine while I’m sleeping at night so it doesn’t matter if it takes 1 hour or 4. I suppose having to carry a micro usb cord and charger when other devices use a usb-c cord/charger may be annoying but I think I can find 2 square inches in my purse/pocket/bag/backpack for it.

Also remember that this is an e-reader. It’s not a tablet, computer or smartphone, nor does it make any claims to be. Expecting an ereader to function basically like a computer/tablet/smartphone is expecting too much. It does an outstanding job at doing it’s job as an ereader.

I have sent many different type of files to my Paperwhite using my kindle email address and it’s worked excellent with that old ereader, so I expect this new Oasis will do excellent with those as well.

My suggestion is to read the description fully and know what you are getting and what you aren’t.
If your reading experience will be destroyed because this doesn’t have (nor claim to have) a usb-c, then this isn’t the ereader for you.
If you want it to be like a tablet or smartphone or computer, this isn’t the ereader for you.

But if you love reading and buy this for what it’s made for, I can recommend it.
Definitely look into getting a discount by trading in any unused kindles, and take advantage of the free Kindle Unlimited and Audible while they are available to offset the cost even more.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Oasis – With 7” display and page turn buttons- Ad-Supported + 3 Months Free Kindle Unlimited (with auto-renewal)

For the price, I would have expected better in that department.

The strongest plus to these headphones is the clarity of the music. Even with the lower volume and the lack of bass, the music is sharp and clear - something I have found gets lost with other brands. The noise cancellation is also a strength above others.

Overall, I would recommend if you’re not searching for heavily bassed or volumed headphones.

text_fidelity_a:
Bose CineMate 1 SR Home Theater Speaker System (Black) I bought this system to replace my Yamaha YSP-500 and a fairly sizeable subwoofer. My issue was that we were doing a remodel of our living room to put in a wall with a fireplace and stonework where our existing entertainment center was. Because the Yamaha projector is fairly substantial, mounting it directly to the wall wasn't an option, so I would have had to build another shelf or do something else. I would have also had to relocate the sub which would have meant either buying some sort of wireless set up or running a cable under the floor and into the wall.

Since the Bose speaker is much slimmer and lighter, has an available wall bracket, and the sub is wireless I thought I had the solution to my problem. For that part, the Bose is great. It was easy to mount, is relatively unobtrusive, and having more flexibility with the placement of the sub is really nice. If you have space limitations or just don't want to mess with running speaker wire (or can't) then this is a good alternative.

This is also a good alternative for people that just want to plug something in and have it work. If you are technically challenged, or just don't want to invest the time in setting up a home theater then this is a usable solution. Most people could have this up and running (including configuration) in less than 20 minutes.

I thought the sound quality is pretty decent. I don't know that it is significantly better than the older (and cheaper) Yamaha Sound Projector that it replaced. Unlike some reviewers, I thought voices (at least on television shows) were clearer and easier to hear than what I was used to. The bass was crisp, but I haven't experienced the punch I am used to with my Yamaha sub. Granted the Bose Accoustimass module is a lot smaller, but there is a very noticeable difference.

There are two areas that I took a star away for each. One is obviously cost. At around $1000, I would say that this would be a better value. At its current price I think that you are not really getting what you pay for. For all the trade-offs, I think there are cheaper alternatives.

The second is the fact that it lacks any sort of display or ability to customize. You can't make any sort of sound profiles (movies, sports, etc), you don't have anything like a night mode, and there is no display whatsoever to indicate something as simple as volume level. Some people may like that, but to me it was rather annoying. For the price, I think you should be able to do a little more with it. Again, if you are the plug-and-play type, this probably won't bother you.

Overall, other than the size and wireless sub, this is not an improvement from my Yamaha Sound Projector. I think it's good, but if I had to do it over again I would probably look at other, cheaper options.
text_fidelity_b: Bose CineMate 1 SR Home Theater Speaker System (Black)

Acer Chromebook, 11.6-Inch, CB3-111-C670 (Intel Celeron, 2GB, 16GB SSD, White) **Discontinued by Manufacturer** I'm typing this review on this Chromebook right now! I'm a graduate student, and I got tired of my Windows computer installing updates every time I opened my laptop. It was frustrating. I just wanted to open my laptop and get right to writing my homework. Now I can! It's also very lightweight, so I can easily bring it and all my books with me to class. It holds a charge for at least 2-3 days of active homework use and general internet fun for me. It starts up almost instantly when I open it! The screen size is fine, and I often have two windows open at the same time, side by side. I've been trying to read more articles online without printing them, and using online textbooks via my Kindle app. After a bit of a learning curve, this has worked out awesome, because if I have my Chromebook, I have ALL my textbooks with me, plus my course information, and my notebook to write things down. I love it. Plus, it doesn't get hot or make a whirring sound when you use it for a long time. I like that because I often use mine while I"m sitting on the couch.

Getting used to using the Chromebook had some hiccups. First, I recommend using Google Docs for writing because it has an offline mode. The Windows OneDrive and cloud version of Word works ok, but if your internet has any interruption, you can't keep typing. That's annoying. So use Google Docs, and don't worry about it! (But if you're working on a project with someone, and they use Word on a Windows laptop, you can collaborate with them no problem using the cloud version of Word.) Second, organizing my files confused me, until I realized that "Save As" is now "Move to folder.' Also, you can download a few files to your Chromebook, so if you need to upload an attachment to Blackboard, you can pretty easily. You'll use your Google Drive for much of your file storage. I did connect my OneDrive to my Chromebook, but it's through a third party app thing, and the connection always has to be redone, so I don't really rely on that, and I plan to move my OneDrive stuff to my Google drive soon.

The only thing that was really hard was setting up my Chromebook to print to my WiFi printer. Google cloud print is in beta, and in theory, it's awesome. When you're done setting it up, you could print to your home printer from anywhere, using your mobile device. However, Google your printer and how to set up cloud print, and give yourself some time to set it up. If you're in a rush, you should just plug your printer into your Chromebook.

Lastly, since many public schools are going Chromebook, I thought it was a good idea to get one myself. I'm working on getting my Master of Arts in Teaching to be an elementary/middle school teacher. Using one for my own schoolwork helps me be able to help students use their Chromebooks. Additionally, the price is so nice, I don't worry about having to ever replace my Chromebook, because if it was damaged by schoolchildren, I'd only be out about $160 (instead of $2000 for a Mac). I'm even thinking of getting one for my mom, since most of what she does online could be done on a Chromebook, too.

Oh, and one very last thing, the keyboard is really enjoyable to type on. The keys are spaced comfortably, and the individual keys make a nice clicky sound, are springy, and are nice and thin, for fast typing. I know that might sound weird, but I'm picky about my keyboards.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Chromebook, 11.6-Inch, CB3-111-C670 (Intel Celeron, 2GB, 16GB SSD, White) **Discontinued by Manufacturer**

I have gone through a couple of these.

What I do like is the charging case. It is pretty slim, it is USB C, and it also has a display to show how much of a charge it has. This is super helpful. It also has volume and connect/disconnect buttons. This has not yet had any charging issues, but I have not owned it for very long.

Now for what I don't like- They do not fit my ear that well. It may be the shape of hook, the length of the arm from which the speaker is mounted, or some other variable. The hook keeps it in place, but it never feels as if it's in my ear properly. I also think the sound is not so hot, and for 50 dollars I was expecting more. It is a little treble heavy on the heavier frequencies and just sounds like a cheap driver.

My previous headphone was the MPow Flame Lite. The charging case is bulkier and bare and there is no digital display. With that said- these are now 1/3 of the price. What I do like is that they fit my ear like a glove, and the sound quality is phenominal. It sounds like a much bigger driver. I am not an audiophile, but it really sounds great. Maybe it is the mid that come in fuller giving it a rich sound.

I have had some charging issues. Sometimes I find that only one of the headphones are dead and the other is fully charged. However, fit and sound are my most important details so these are my favorite. For the price I can purchase three and keep them in different places. If I lose one or have a charging issue I can replace it with the extra. This makes much more sense than keeping the aI do not more.

Edit: I changed from 3 to 5 stars. I have owned these now for almost one year, and use them probably every day. There has been no decrease in performance or battery life. I was so accustomed to my previous ear buds that I did not like these much at first. However, the sound is balanced, the battery life is great, and I really like the charging case. I have never actually times the batter life, but it is probably about 7-8 hours on a full charge. There are sooo many choices now for bluetooth ear buds, but these are a safe bet and most people should be happy. I am however not an audiophile, and someone who truly is may want to spend more on a Bose, or whatever the best ear buds are nowadays. My previous ones were more bass heavy, but these are better balanced. They do stay in the ear, unless I go to lay down on my back; I then have to push them back into my ear.

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Touch, Wi-Fi, 6" E Ink Display - includes Special Offers & Sponsored Screensavers I tried the first generation Kindle but didn't really care all that much for it. While I loved the screen, it just didn't feel right, and remember thinking this would be perfect if it had a touchscreen.

When the Touch was announced I ordered this along with a Fire with the thought that the Fire would be for me, and I'd give the Touch as a gift. The Touch got here this morning and I opened it up just to make sure it was OK. It looked so nice that I carefully peeled off the plastic just to try it out for a few minutes. After all, one wouldn't want to give a gift that didn't work, right? Well, it's now been a few hours and several chapters of a few books later. I'm keeping it. A second one will be on order for Christmas giving.

Why keep the Touch when I also have a Fire? If you skip over the obvious answer (I just love electronic gadgets) the e-ink on the Touch is much better in terms of clarity and lack of glare. Not that the Fire is bad. It has a very clear screen, but there is some glare. The Touch is better for reading under all lighting situations, and remains highly readable in direct sun. I can't imagine getting better screen clarity than this for black and white text.

I also tried reading it while on a treadmill (a situation that usually gives me a headache when I tried it using the kindle app on my Touchpad) and it was quite pleasant. Best of all is that I can zoom up the text size so I can read it while it is on the treadmill reading stand (it's too far away for me to read hard copy unless it's in HUGE type. Getting old is _not_ fun).

But the strength of the Touch is also it's biggest problem for me - black and white. I read several magazines each month and reading them in B/W is lackluster at best. Magazines are more enjoyable on the Fire, especially publications such as Wired.

The touch interface is great. So far its been very smooth and glitch free. Love the feel of the screen - has a bit of texture to it. I have to say, however, that I am a bit concerned about the screen longevity. The Touch overall feels a bit fragile and less "solid" than the Fire. I'm not deducting any stars for that since it's just an impression, but it will be interesting to see if the durability of the Touch screen is better/worse/same as the Fire (and vice versa). I'll be getting a case for it for sure since it's going to be getting bumped about.

I'll be using the Fire mainly at home and for reading material that works best in color (and, of course, video - need to relax the mind with mindless entertainment as well!). The Touch will be living in my briefcase for reading while commuting (I take the bus and subway, so lots of time to read) and for killing time prior to an appointment. The longer battery life and smaller size makes it a better traveling companion than the Fire. I don't have the Touch 3G version, so I'll have to make sure I keep a few books on my to-be-read stack so I don't run out when I'm out of wi-fi range.

Granted, if I could only have one device, I'd stay with the Fire since that offers more entertainment options, albeit at twice the price. But the cost is not excessive, so I treated myself to both. With a Fire and a Touch I've got all bases covered (until, of course, the next glittery gee-whiz piece of electronics comes out...).
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Touch, Wi-Fi, 6" E Ink Display - includes Special Offers & Sponsored Screensavers

Spent 2 hours on the phone with a Kasa tech rep today. My hub no longer works so cameras not working remotedly. Contacted Amazon for a refund - just received these cameras TODAY. Amazon has a new policy for returning tech so make certain you understand what that is before you try to return a non-refundable item.

------------------------------------------

Easy to set up. Pictures / video crystal clear. Use them as wildlife cameras. One set up outside dryer vent where Carolina wrens set up nest with 7 eggs (venting the dryer out of the window until they hatch and fledge).

Others hanging in yard by various feeders to get close up of woodpeckers. Nuthatches. Etc. Can’t wait to hang one by hummingbird feeders. When squirrels climb my feeder I hit the siren. Wireless is the way to go. Hanging and operating 24/7 for over a week now. 97% battery remaining.

Hub inside kitchen and is 50’ away from one camera and 90’ away from another. Works beautifully. I pay the $3 a month for Kasa video storage until I can view and save or delete.

Have over a dozen Kasa devices around my home. Love all.
text_fidelity_b: Kasa Home Security Camera System Wireless Outdoor & Indoor Camera by TP-Link, 1080P HD with Siren, Night Vision, Battery Rechargeable, Magnetic Wall Mount, Works w/Alexa & Google Home (KC300S2)

text_fidelity_a:
Altec Lansing Comfort Q+ Bluetooth Headphones, Active Noise Cancellation, Comfortable, Quite, Noise Cancelling Headphone, Up to 26 Hours of Playtime, 30 Ft. Wireless Range, Rose Gold These are a nice set of headphones, look-wise. They don't look cheap, fold up well and are fairly comfortable once you get them fitted right. I was getting some ear pain at first, but extended the top a bit and they now fit comfortably.

The bluetooth connected easily and easily allows me to go into the next room and still listen to my iPad that is more centrally located to pick up the wifi. Great for when I'm cleaning and want to listen to podcasts or YouTube. It charged fairly quickly and has lasted about a week of non-continual use. When the charge ran out, I was still able to hear by plugging in the phones into the audio until I had time to recharge.

Now the noise cancelling. It works. Our A/C unit sits outside the family room and is very noisy when running. I put on the NC and it was gone. Only problem was a static sound that popped up periodically. It wasn't continuous but loud enough to be annoying when it did. It may not be an issue for someone else, but it caused me to ding it a star. I haven't yet tried these on an airplane, which is where I normally use noise cancelling. But base on how it worked with the A/C, I expect these will do a great job. Just don't expect it to wipe out outside noise. I could still hear the TV going and my husband talking. Just no A/C loud rumbling noise. Now if only I could sleep in these to kill the sound of my husband's fan.

I did get these free in exchange for my honest opinion. What is funny is a just bought a new pair of noise cancelling headphones because my old ones just died and I like these better so far....
text_fidelity_b: Altec Lansing Comfort Q+ Bluetooth Headphones, Active Noise Cancellation, Comfortable, Quite, Noise Cancelling Headphone, Up to 26 Hours of Playtime, 30 Ft. Wireless Range, Rose Gold

text_fidelity_a:
Panasonic DMP-BD87 Ultra-Fast Booting Blu-ray Disc Player When we first tried it, the streaming was awful. It couldn't hold a connection to Vudu, to Hulu, or to Netflix.

We ran an update--tricky because it didn't readily hold a solid network connection--and things improved considerably. I can stream Hulu with minor hiccups, Netflix without issues, and Vudu except at 1080p. For the record, I can stream Vudu at 1080p on the TV that the player is connected to. It still supports only a small subset of services, though Hulu has been added. As a streaming media player, it doesn't meet expectations. As a simple blu-ray player, it is quite excellent for the price. It was able to play a few old, slightly scratched DVDs that other players were having trouble loading.

On the signature features, I could find no appreciable difference in boot up or launch time between this and my Sony, or between this with fast boot turned on and this with fast boot turned off. Blu-ray players tend to boot pretty fast in any case. This one allows up to four users to have customized interfaces, but it only affects the background image and color scheme of the interface screen. It does not allow four users to each maintain their own login to Netflix or Hulu, which would be useful if Netflix ever allowed multiple users of an account to maintain their own Watch Instantly queue the way they do with DVD queues.
text_fidelity_b: Panasonic DMP-BD87 Ultra-Fast Booting Blu-ray Disc Player

They also look pretty okay. The fact that they fold flat is a nice little bonus but for a pair of utility headphones, I think these are a home run.

They're too flimsy to call a solid pair, but for casually listening to music while multi-tasking at home or for watching a streaming video, these do just great. text_fidelity_a:
RayHom 8 Bay AA AAA Battery Charger, Double Charging Speed with LCD Display Independent Slot for Ni-MH AA AAA Rechargeable Batteries This is a nice alternative to chargers that require you to charge batteries in pairs. There are spaces for eight batteries, and you can charge any number within them, and mix and match AA and AAA. The eight spaces are divided electrically into two banks of four spaces, and the manufacturer says each bank can provide 2000 mA of charging power (which lowers as you add more batteries and the current is divided between them). However, the included adapter only provides only 1200 mA (so says its label), so I'm not sure the math checks out.

I gave it a test with an assortment of different brand and capacity rechargeables, then checked the batteries with a multimeter. Even fully loaded the charger worked pretty quickly and brought each one up to just over 1.4 volts. I have a brand-name charger that will bring them up to 1.5 volts, but that may be overcharging a bit and might reduce overall battery life.

The one minor negative is that the battery icons on the backlit display are pretty much invisible unless you bend down or tilt the charger up to see them. You can see how low the angle is in the photo I uploaded.

Other than that, convenient and reasonably fast, it's a nice charger.
text_fidelity_b: RayHom 8 Bay AA AAA Battery Charger, Double Charging Speed with LCD Display Independent Slot for Ni-MH AA AAA Rechargeable Batteries

text_fidelity_a: Google WiFi system, 3-Pack - Router Replacement for Whole Home Coverage (NLS-1304-25),White Easy to setup and works like a charm @ first. Until it didn't. O.k. I must say I know enough about mesh networks to be dangerous but I must say something from the very beginning with the mesh system was strange. Alright it all started back at the beginning of the year where at certain times of night my internet would drag. I said, "NIGHT." Typically in the morning when everyone else is sleep. I am up working. I would notice download speeds of maybe about 25 and uploads at 10. So after a few days of this,  I contacted Xfinity internet support and ask them to run a check on the internet. Right away, the support guy said, "Log into your account and let me show you something."  I said O.k. and right there I am seeing the traffic go thru the roof. The rep said, "Oh yes there is a lot of traffic on for some reason coming from Somalia. I said are you sure. He said Oh yes.  Since I run a business I have backup internet thru another company that I can jump on in case my internet goes down.  So I disconnected my internet and and change the wifi mesh name and password. Later that morning, I noticed that the ssid was still broadcasting my old ssid name so I connected too it and noticed that I still had internet.  REALLY!!!!! I could watch movies and everything. Very strange. So I contacted Google support and was told to reset the mesh back to the original factory systems. Now for the last 4 to 5 months I have to change my ssid every few months and reset everything back to factory settings to keep my internet from dragging. I haven't read anything else about this expect a few bloggers and you-tubers say that they suspect that the mesh network can be hacked.  I must say after a few months of tracking my internet usage online I must say I suspect the same. If you purchase this check your usage regularly.  I have owned this mesh system since 2017 and didn't notice any problems until recently. Trying a new mesh network. It think it is time.
text_fidelity_b: Google WiFi system, 3-Pack - Router Replacement for Whole Home Coverage (NLS-1304-25),White

text_fidelity_a:
3DConnexion 3DX-700059 Spacemouse Compact 3D Mouse At first I was skeptical about the idea of using my left hand for this. I was initially expecting it to be a replacement mouse for my right hand, but after more research I understood what they are trying to do. I must say that it's much easier to use than I expected, and operating it with my left hand works just fine.

I was also hesitant because of the price. However, this mouse is fantastic. Worth every penny. I'm using it with SketchUp, and it's vastly easier and faster than the normal built-in navigation tools. It's hard to articulate just how awesome this is. Once you get used to it, it's instinctive and effortless, and moving around the model is so easy! You will absolutely love it.

There was one tricky thing during the setup, however. I plugged it in, loaded the driver, and launched SketchUp. Then I found and opened the configuration window to customize it for SketchUp. The info I had found showed that configuration window with "SketchUp" at the top, and the SketchUp-specific options. But my configuration window didn't have anything specific to SketchUp. It said Windows Explorer at the top instead of SketchUp. I thought I was missing a driver. I messed around a log time, and looked through lots of online info.

At one point, I noticed it said Chrome instead of Windows Explorer. That's when I figured it out. The configuration window changes by itself, based on what application is active. I had SketchUp running in the background, but my most recent activity was with Windows Explorer and then Chrome. With the configuration window open, I clicked over into the SketchUp window, and suddenly the configuration window said SketchUp at the top, and the the SketchUp-specific settings appeared. I wish that had been in the instructions somewhere!!

At first I didn't bother programming the buttons, but later I tried it, and that's an awesome feature. For Sketchup, I programmed one button to be "remove guides", and the other is "paste in place". Hitting those buttons is much faster than finding those things in the menu each time. However, I discovered that I need to make sure I'm not moving through the model when I press the "paste in place" button, or the mouse locks up, and I need to restart SketchUp. But as long as I make sure I'm not moving when I press it, I never have that problem anymore.

Anyway, you will absolutely love this. After using it, I no longer had any doubt about it being worth the money. It's worth every penny. I would give it 6 stars if I could.
text_fidelity_b: 3DConnexion 3DX-700059 Spacemouse Compact 3D Mouse

text_fidelity_a:
HUION Inspiroy H1060P Graphics Drawing Tablet with 8192 Pressure Sensitivity Battery-Free Stylus and 12 Customized Hot Keys, 10 x 6.25 inches Digital Art Tablet for Mac, Windows PC and Android *UPDATED*
After a year of use. The tablet canvas started chipping in the middle of the protective coating. Stylus pressure and positioning still work but it's annoying as heck plus not it's even chipping more every time I go over same spot. I've never had that happen with any of the Huion & Wacom tablets I've owned for more years than this. I also can't seem to find a tablet protector for this either. So kind of bummed because I really like this...or want to really like this tablet.

*Original review*
First off, just like Wacoms these Huions are compatible with literally all major art software programs as well as budget programs.
I personally have used this Huion with Photoshop, Illustrator, 3D Studio Max, Zbrush, Mudbox, 3D Coat, Substance Painter, Clip Art Studio (Manga Studio), Krita, Painter, Paint Too Sai....can't remember the rest.
This NEW HUION 1060 PLUS is ASIN# B01FTE9HS2 and it comes with a stylus holder, 4 stylus nibs, a carrying case and drawing glove.
There is also another NEW version I saw on Amazon which includes 10 stylus nibs, holder and a glove without carrying case but they are the same exact tablet. They are both the same price on Amazon as of this writing.
Not to get you confused but there is an older one also called the 1060 Plus but it is not labled NEW or UPGRADED.
It is different cosmetically and has older technology and features.
The NEW 1060 Plus has Full-Area Surface Cover and Thinner Border, which makes the drawing surface bigger plus an attached side holder for stylus. Also, Quieter Express Keys, Better Linearity in art programs, Better pen pressure sensitivity.
(Specifications: Resolution: 5080 LPI, Report Rate: 233 RPS, 2048 Levels of Pressure, 10" x 6.25" active area.)
*Note: I just found out they released an even newer one with smoother pressure/linearity and has 8192 levels of pressure but it costs a little bit more.*

Now to the good stuff. Drivers were easy to install and worked right away; which is surprising because I've had driver issues with every non-Wacom tablets in the past. Actually, there are rare hiccups where the USB wouldn't recognize the tablet so I just have to replug back in. I've even had that issue with wacoms so I would just have to reconnect the USB back in to get it to recognize. Another common issue with older tablets (even Wacom) is that with Photoshop sometimes doesn't register the pressure sensitivity so I would have to either restart Photoshop or reconnect the USB.
But other than the super rare hiccups, this tablet looks very professional and is an great upgrade from the Huion H610 Pro, which I own, plus the Huion GT 220 graphics tablet which similar to the Wacom 22HD but way better IPS picture quality. I own the Wacom 22HD Touch and is totally not worth the $2000 I spent compared to the $700 I bought the Huion GT220 for. The Huion GT220 may have not come with express keys but I never use those awkward positioned keys anyways. I prefer the keyboard or game pad. I also owned a Wacom Intuos 2, Wacom Intuos 4 and an Intuos 4 Wireless which I've used throughout my professional career as an artist. (I wanted to compare them to see if a lower cost alternative is worth the savings). But my recommendation is if you are already an artist or aspiring to be an artist, don't hesitate on getting the tablet that gives you the best bang for your buck. Wacom does have good build but drivers can be flakey too. I've had some Wacoms stop recognizing the drivers to the point where I have to reinstall it.
With the 1060 PLUS you're pretty much set with a drawing tablet if you can't afford a Wacom or Surface Pro for all your 3D, drawing and painting needs. And to me, the pressure curve and sensitivity is feels equal to, if not better than, the Wacom tablets.

This Huion is the best bang for you buck for aspiring artist that want a professional tablet at the best price. I don't want to stray anyone away from a Wacom if they can afford it. But it's great to know that you can now save 1/5 the cost of a Wacom with the similar, if not better, specifications.
Actually, I purchased 5 of these for us artists at work and also had to recently recommend this Huion to my friends and family looking for a tablet for their kids that are also aspiring artist and animators. They showed me their kids' drawings and animation with the mouse I convinced their parents to get a drawing tablet. It is a must have for artists but you don't need to spend an arm and a leg. I truly believe this is the best $80 price range tablet on the market today that runs on Windows 10 (as of this writing). It has worked well for me for my professional (and personal) work with 3D sculpting, drawing and painting. Sorry Wacom....$250 to $300 for a comparable mid-size tablet is not aspiring artist friendly. They may look a bit cooler but they all achieve the same end. They also have Wacom Bamboos or budget Wacoms under $70 but they all lack the pressure sensitivity and features with only 1024 levels of sensitivity. I'm not a Huion salesman but this just makes sense and achieves the same end.....which is quality art without frustrating hardware and features.
text_fidelity_b: HUION Inspiroy H1060P Graphics Drawing Tablet with 8192 Pressure Sensitivity Battery-Free Stylus and 12 Customized Hot Keys, 10 x 6.25 inches Digital Art Tablet for Mac, Windows PC and Android

text_fidelity_a:
Polaroid Cube+ 1440p Mini Lifestyle Action Camera with Wi-Fi & Image Stabilization (Red) I really hate to use the word “cute” but there’s no way around it – this is a cute cam! It looks pretty much the same as the original Cube, but offers improved video and the addition of WiFi. Of the new features, the WiFi is the most significant, and makes this far more useful as a cam.

I also have the original Cube and the build quality continues to be very good. These are priced higher than the “no name” action cams, but after using (and breaking) a couple of those, it’s nice to be able to count on the Cube to keep on working. It’s water resistant, which makes it less worrisome when using it in bad weather or around water. It supports up to a 128MB SD card

The form factor and overall design is much the same as the original Cube. It has a magnet in the base that is more than strong enough to keep it well-planted. It’s not strong enough for significant activity (e.g., staying on a bike handle while riding) but it offers the benefit of tripod-like stability without the need for a tripod (providing you have something metal to fasten the magnet).

The biggest change is wifi on the Cube+. I found the setup to be straightforward – basically just download the app and follow the setup steps. I love that the app lets you use it as a live view – that’s a big improvement over the original Cube. It’s a very helpful feature for planning a shot, plus allows me to monitor how things are turning out without having to play the video.

Image quality has been impressive – zero complaints there. I was pleased with the resolution of the original Cube, and this is a bit better. Audio quality is OK. It’s not outstanding, but it clearly picks up voices. I understand that earlier versions of the Cube+ had very poor sound quality, but the one I have (got it in Dec 2015) is fine with regard to sound.

All in all, it’s a great cam with a fun form factor and look. Well worth considering if you’re looking for a small profile action cam with solid build quality and performance. While the price has increased over that of the original Cube, the wifi features are very useful and well implemented, making this version well worth the additional cost.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Polaroid Cube+ 1440p Mini Lifestyle Action Camera with Wi-Fi & Image Stabilization (Red)

text_fidelity_a: VideoSecu ML12 TV Wall Mount Articulating Arm Monitor Bracket for Most 19"-32" LCD LED Plasma Flat Panel Screen TV with VESA 100x100mm 75x75mm B0E Plenty stout to hold a 21" monitor with no noticable sag.  The tilt feature is very nice.  Installation was simple enough; I didn't have a stud where I wanted it, so fixed a piece of finished wood about an inch bigger in all dimensions than the wall-mount bracket using drywall anchors, then screwed the arm to that.  Leveling was simple, the bottom hole is elongated to allow some adjustments.  The torpedo level magnet sticks to the arm, so you have both hands free to make sure the arm is level, tightenign the screw with one hand while applying whatever push is needed to keep the arm level until the bottom screw is tight.  The allen-wrench that comes with the bag of screws can be used to tighten or loosen the adjustment screws at the shoulder/elbow/wrist, but I didn't need to use it.  The adjustments were tight enough and didn't move once the monitor was where I wanted it.  The two big screws to hold it to the wall are black, but the small screws that hold the monitor to the arm (they come with the kit) are silver-colored rather than black; so the monitor is black, and the arm is black, but the screws are metal color.  But who looks at the back of the thing?  I'd buy another any time.

text_fidelity_a:
IPOW 360 Degree Rotatable Break-Resistant iPad Tripod Mount Adapter, Universal Tablet Clamp Holder Fits Ipad, Ipad Air, Pro, Mini, Microsoft Surface, Nexus, for Tripod Monopod, Selfie Stick,Tabletop What a great idea! When I saw this CD slot mounting thing, I was thrilled to be given one in return for an honest review. We have resisted getting a smart phone for long time because of the price but recently signed up for an account with Spring and got a Samsung Galaxy 6 as part of the deal. But the idea of doing some kind of cumbersome mount in the car was not appealing, especially after our experience with a GPS unit several years ago that we never used because all the mounts we tried were awful and more trouble than they were worth.

This mounted perfectly, and securely, in the CD slot (which we very rarely use), but it would also mount in a vent slot if wide enough. You can adjust the direction and angle of your device until you get it how it works best for you, then tighten everything down to lock it in.

The printed instructions are good, but the one thing they don't tell you is not to be timid about it. The piece that holds the device (with the notches) snaps onto what they refer to as "the outstanding round stick," which is the knob/ball bearing part of the holder. At first I thought it was not going to fit, but then I realized I needed to push on it fairly firmly to get it to snap to the ball. After that, you can move the device holder around at varying angles to get it like you want it, then tighten down the big round screw that fits between the two pieces to lock the position.

I also wasn't totally clear on how the CD/vent slot part was supposed to mount, thinking it would shove up inside the CD player like a CD would. It doesn't. It fits in a little ways, not far, and then you turn the triangular-headed screw to raise up the plate until it is wide enough to hold it firmly. It works well, and it doesn't damage your CD player at all. The device holder also takes forceful pulling to widen it to accommodate your device, so you should put your device into it before putting the whole thing into the CD or vent slot. It will snap back snugly against the device, so be careful not to release it too quickly. Once the mount is installed in the slot, if you need to adjust the angle, you can by loosening the round screw slightly and making the adjustment. Our CD slot is up at the top of the dashboard, so the phone is positioned up closer to eye level so we can look at the phone while driving more easily. If your CD slot is down low, you might want to use a vent slot instead.

What I really love about this product is how neat and tidy it is. It solves a problem, and it does it inexpensively and without looking shoddy. A very nice, creative product for cellphone or small GPS users.
text_fidelity_b: IPOW 360 Degree Rotatable Break-Resistant iPad Tripod Mount Adapter, Universal Tablet Clamp Holder Fits Ipad, Ipad Air, Pro, Mini, Microsoft Surface, Nexus, for Tripod Monopod, Selfie Stick,Tabletop

text_fidelity_a:
Linksys N300 Wi-Fi Wireless Router (E900) As a wireless router, this works pretty much like any other, so I thought I'd use it for another purpose: wireless networking between computers in a household that does not have internet (since this is the situation for many people).
For that usage, here's the review:

Appearance: This is a very streamline wireless router with 4 hardline ports. It's small and flat, good for a desk. The problems I have with the design are that it HAS to lie flat, and you can't mount it on a wall. Depending on how cluttered your desk area is may cause some issues.
-3 out of 5 stars

Setup: This router comes with a generic setup CD which assists not so tech savvy users to setup their wireless network using minor cables and a CD. During the CD installation it has "Show Me" buttons to assist users on actions they need to take. A large problem with this router is that you can't setup the router without an active internet connection. I attempted to use the 192.168.1.1 to manually setup the router without using the CD and was met with obstruction requiring me to run their software. This would be a bad router for local home groups without an internet connection. Attempted to connect wirelessly and was granted access to setup things like the security to connect, the security options are minor and only seem to allow WPA2-Personal security with the standard AES encryption. Because this is intended more for internet than networking, this won't count much against the overall product, so
-3 out of 5

Usability: I did the connection with my laptop and walked around to see if the signal would drop. I made it out to the street corner from where the router was placed, this was about 200ft. I still received a single bar signal out at the corner. A recommendation for the router if you are using it to broadcast an internet signal that it is password protected using both letters UPPERCASE and lowercase with numbers and symbols. This will help protect your network and any data stored on your computers. Even though the range on this router was pretty good the minor security options make it difficult to give it above a 3 out of 5.
-3 out of 5

Reliability: I attempted to reset the router back to factory by resetting it and letting it sit for about 15minutes. The router kept all information including the Name and the Password. This is both good and bad if there is a short power outage you don't have to worry about resetting passwords and the router information however if you ever lose your password you might not be able to restore it back to factory.
-3 out of 5
text_fidelity_b: Linksys N300 Wi-Fi Wireless Router (E900)
