Lexar JumpDrive S73 64GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive LJDS73-64GASBNA (Green) I'm not going to bother with a detailed listing of times as many other reviewers have done a nice job with that. I'll just say that I did time out this device in comparison to a pair of my 2.0 flashdrives and another 3.0 on a pair of Macs, one with 2.0 USB and one with 3.0 USB. There's no doubt it's speedier in all cases than my 2.0s, whether I was transferring over a folder with a lot of docs or a folder with mixed media (docs, photos, video). Roughly 2-3 times as fast than 2.0 consistently (that's with both of them in the 2.0 ports), though the gap narrowed with really large, mixed folders. When it goes into the 3.0, it was consistently 3-4 times faster, with again a narrower gap with really large, mixed files. In comparison to a Triton, it was definitely significantly and noticeably slower, a little bit better than half as fast.

The device feels very light and the casing not quite as sturdy as my other drives, though I never feel like it's in danger of breaking. Just doesn't have the same sense of heft and durability.

On the other hand, the slide clicks in nicely and solid, with a satisfying sound and doesn't retract easily unless you are wanting it to

If you have a 2.0 drive, it'll be noticeably faster and if you're looking for a drive, makes sense to get one that can go with you to your next upgrade. If you've upgraded to 3.0 and want a new drive just for that, there's no doubt you'll notice the difference, and especially with large files and movies etc. I'd ay it's definitely worth it. As for going beyond to the Triton, personally my need for speed isn't that great--this one would suit me fine. Some people though have less patience than I do. Plus, I'm cheap. So slower than the other 3.0, but I'd say still a fine value.
text_fidelity_b: Lexar JumpDrive S73 64GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive LJDS73-64GASBNA (Green)

After break-in, these MEE buds were sounding like something that cost 4-5 times as much with a nice, even frequency response that favors bass only slightly. I find them comparable to $60-$80 Sennheisers, my previous favorites (which superseded Sony and Koss buds that I also liked). These MEE buds came with 3 sets (S, M, and L) of your typical soft rubber earpieces as well as 2 sets of the interesting multi-tiered earpieces shown in the photos and a pretty standard cloth case. Between the various earpiece options, it's unlikely anyone will have an issue finding a good fit.

The cord is about 1 m long, which suits my purposes. I like the over-the-ear wire bits, too, as they prevent tugs on the cord from dislodging them. They might be awkward with some kinds of glasses, but my straight-earpiece sunglasses fit over them fine. They can be bent to hang down more like normal earbuds if desired, though.

I'll be checking out more MEE products now, seeing what a great value these were. I still favor AKG and Beyerdynamic at the high end, but for my biking/hiking/running/workout listening needs, I'll probably be coming back to MEE.

And while the primary goal is as a fitness watch, which it excels at, I really get a kick out of the fact that I can get all my push notifications on it, and even read emails and texts on it.
But back to Fitness. Of course, it acts as a pedometer. But it also measures your heartbeat, every 5 minutes. This thing keeps track of everything! It even knows what kind of exercise you're doing. It maps out progress so that it's easier to keep an eye on where your goals are and how to meet them.
It's synced to my Samsung Galaxy phone, and it plays all of the music that I've got on my phone.

While it is not waterproof, it is water resistant. I'm one of those people that washes my hands a lot, and I haven't had any problem with water sprinkling on it.
Right now I split my time between two locations. The GPS works great in the Midwest, yet is pretty dicey in Wyoming. Since that isn't a big issue for me, no star is subtracted. This is a quality product that does all I want it to do, and more.

Between that, the higher cost, and a few other things, I'm in the market for a different tablet and computer.

In the past, the problem switching back was that, unlike with Apple, things were not quite as user friendly with the interface and you had to really figure things out instead of it being immediately apparent.

Happily, it was different with this tablet. Out of the box, my family and I were able to figure it out quickly and easily, giving us hope in another option.

Quality: Great image on the screen with very high resolution! The feel of the device is also sturdy, aesthetically pleasing, lightweight, and thin.

User-friendly layout, very accessible, good features, and it works seamlessly with Google. I've got google email and YouTube channels, so it's nice to know there's a trade-off for losing some of the other things like seamless transitions between iTunes, my current calendar (not in love with that--I can just as easily switch to google or droid for this)...

All this adds up to the following: Apple can no longer claim to be the clear leader in tablets, phones, and computers. They have stopped innovating far beyond comparable products, and now, for the value and overall performance, the ZenPad is a worthy adversary.

I still have my MacBook Pro computer, but when it comes time to buy a new one, I will be ready to switch knowing items like these are available.
What a great surprise!
text_fidelity_b: ASUS ZenPad 3S 10 9.7" (2048x1536), 4GB RAM, 64GB eMMC, 5MP Front / 8MP Rear Camera, Android 6.0, Tablet, Glacier Silver (Z500M-C1-SL)
